svg.text: Caching in fux -- one plane, two writers, two readers
No new cache. Python's .fux/runtime/ IS the shared cache;
Node learns to read it, and to build it byte for byte.
0 - THE ONLY INPUT: THE COMMITTED INDEX. NOTHING IN .fux/runtime/ FEEDS ANYTHING BUT A QUERY.
257 shards, 38 MB on this repo. One line per document: right for git, wrong for querying.
The build reads these and nothing else, so the plane is deletable at any moment.
1 - TWO WRITERS, ONE LOCK, ONE OUTPUT
Asserts both raw-byte invariants per record; refuses to build.
Same input, same invariants, same refusals. No read verb ever builds.
O_CREAT|O_EXCL, pid JSON (SR-LOCKS). One writer at a time, whichever runtime.
2 - THE PLANE: .fux/runtime/ -- GITIGNORED, DISPOSABLE. PYTHON'S LAYOUT IS THE CONTRACT; NO FILE CHANGES.
id -> loc, title, flen, archived, mtime, alen
n and RAW total_flen -- never weighted
the graph plane. Node rebuilds it instead -- Fork A
schema, docs_fields, a sha per committed shard
[size, mtime_ns] per shard. WRITTEN LAST. The freshness key
Candidates and statistics only -- never a score. Both readers hand what they read to the same rank(), so the plane can make a query fast and cannot make it different.
schema and docs_fields match, shard count matches, and every
shard's [size, mtime_ns] equals stamp.json. Stat only -- no hashing.
The same test, transcribed. mtime_ns is ~1.79e18, past 2^53:
statSync(p, {bigint: true}) or it never matches -- silently.
ranked_by: scan today; accelerator once Tier 1 lands
same ids, same order, scores equal after round(9) -- in all four paths. Not fresh is never an error.
4 - THE REFER PLANE'S CACHES -- SR-CACHE, UNCHANGED. THEY CACHE FETCHES, NOT QUERIES.
In memory, one process. The content
address is IN the key, so a hit is the
fetch's own bytes or it is not a hit.
Retained URL bytes. Node reads them
5 - REFUSED, PARKED, OR OPEN -- named so that an absence is not mistaken for a plan
long key where one missing input
is a silent wrong answer; would
PARKED. Per process, in fux mcp
and fux serve only, one per
runtime, dropped on a new stamp.
NOT PROPOSED. A read verb that
builds is a writer: SR-LOCKS d2.
d9) even when it built the file.
6 - WHAT HOLDS THEM EQUAL -- a second writer is a second thing to keep true
The differential law, extended by W-242
query lanes: Node-plane = Node-scan = Python-plane on candidates, (n, total_wlen, df) and ordering -- this repo, rung-10000, the adversarial index
build lane: diff -r Node-built vs Python-built, excluding stamp.json -- then each runtime answers from the OTHER's plane at 0 discordant
unit binds: one .idx fixture read by both suites · a shard-read counter (Tier 0) · graph.json keeps ensure_ascii + insertion order; the rest sort keys
